timeoutSourceEvidence.timerBehavior: withTimeout rejects its wrapper at deadline and still attaches then handlers to the original test promise. The test body is not forcibly interrupted.
timeoutSourceEvidence.elapsedFallback: On original promise resolution it also rejects if elapsed time meets or exceeds the timeout, because long microtasks may delay the timeout timer.
timeoutSourceEvidence.abortBehavior: Vitest aborts the test context signal on timeout, but these zero-argument async fixture functions do not observe that signal.
timeoutSourceEvidence.importantLimit: The recorded 23s and 73s durations do not identify which timeout path occurred. Cleanup overlap is possible, not proven.

cascadeAssessment.verdict: Plausible but unproven for the pointer assertion
evidence: Pointer failure immediately follows the timed-out lifecycle test in the same isolated file environment.
The lifecycle finally block restores shared global mocks and owned DOM state asynchronously.
resetStemLab resets registry objects and does not itself unmount prior React roots or restore global mocks.
The native pointer guard remains baseline-identical and explicitly ignores a mismatched pointer ID.
cascadeAssessment.limit: Exact source preservation establishes unchanged native handler code. It does not by itself prove that additional rendering work or host scheduling had no effect on timing.

isolatedRetry.argumentHandling: Pass each pattern as one structured child-process argument; do not depend on the broken shell quoting path.
isolatedRetry.deadlineNote: These tests supply explicit timeout arguments to it(). Raising the general --testTimeout flag is not an appropriate way to replace those explicit case budgets.
isolatedRetry.receiptNote: Archive a separate result and run receipt for each fresh process. Report any remaining isolated failure as unresolved rather than attributing it to a cascade.
